records.mechanism: Reactive distributed routing that selects cost-efficient forwarding agents and compensates them with VCG premiums.
records.rationale: The proposed routing protocol selects service providers along a path, coordinates their forwarding and specifies payments to intermediate nodes.

evidence.quote: it guarantees that routing is done along the most cost-efficient path
evidence.rationale: The protocol selects a chain of forwarding service providers on reported forwarding costs.

evidence.quote: we propose Ad hoc-VCG, a reactive routing protocol that achieves the design objectives of truthfulness (i.e., it is in the agents' best interest to reveal their true costs for forwarding data) and cost-efficiency (i.e., it guarantees that routing is done along the most cost-efficient path)
evidence.rationale: The reactive protocol organizes distinct agents' cost reports and dependent forwarding actions along a selected route.

evidence.quote: by paying to the intermediate nodes a premium over their actual costs for forwarding data packets.
evidence.rationale: The mechanism explicitly pays forwarding providers premiums above costs and studies total overpayment; this is a modeled payment rule.

records.adjudication_reason: Adopt B. This is a designed reactive routing protocol arranging mutually dependent forwarding actions by distinct selfish agents, rather than one bidder optimizing its own action. That concrete coordination role supports L3 in addition to the shared L2 provider/path selection and L5 payment findings. Truthfulness is incentive compatibility, so no L1 trust mechanism is inferred.
